description: The image displays five distinct bar charts arranged horizontally, each illustrating a different distribution pattern of parameter allocation across layers in a neural network, as referenced in the context of “Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Design Spaces.” From left to right, the charts are labeled “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck.” Each chart consists of five vertical bars of varying heights, representing relative parameter counts or allocation proportions across five conceptual layers. In the “Increasing” chart, bar heights rise progressively from left to right, starting with the shortest bar on the far left and ending with the tallest on the far right. The “Uniform” chart shows all five bars of equal height, indicating consistent parameter allocation across layers. The “Decreasing” chart mirrors the “Increasing” pattern in reverse, with the tallest bar on the left and progressively shorter bars to the right. The “Spindle” chart features a central peak, with the middle bar being the tallest and bars decreasing in height symmetrically toward both ends. The “Bottleneck” chart has the shortest bar in the center, flanked by progressively taller bars toward the edges, forming a U-shaped or inverted spindle profile. All bars are rendered in a uniform light green color with black outlines, and the x-axis beneath each chart is marked with its respective label in black text. No numerical scales or y-axis labels are provided, so the bar heights are interpreted qualitatively to represent relative magnitudes of parameter distribution.
